items.stem: Explain any six principles of management given by Henri Fayol.
items.answer: (i) Division of work: Work is divided into small tasks done by trained specialists. (ii) Authority and responsibility: Authority and responsibility should be in balance. (iii) Discipline: Obedience to rules and agreements, with good superiors and judicious penalties. (iv) Unity of command: Each employee receives orders from only one superior. (v) Unity of direction: One head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective. (vi) Subordination of individual interest to general interest: The interest of the organisation comes first. (vii) Remuneration of employees: Pay should be just and fair. (viii) Centralisation and decentralisation: A proper balance between the two is needed. (ix) Scalar chain: A formal line of authority from top to bottom, with a gang plank for emergencies. (x) Order: People and materials should be in their proper places. (xi) Equity: Kindness and justice to all employees. (xii) Stability of tenure of personnel: Employees should be retained in their jobs. (xiii) Initiative: Workers should be encouraged to develop and carry out plans. (xiv) Esprit de corps: Team spirit and unity among employees.

items.stem: Which technique of controlling is applied? In each case give a reason. (i) At Bose Agencies, only deviations in material cost above 2% of the standard are reported to the manager. items.stem: Distinguish between Fayol's principles and Taylor's scientific management on the basis of focus, unity of command, expression and basis of formation.
items.answer: (i) Focus: Fayol's principles: improving the overall administration; Taylor's scientific management: increasing productivity. (ii) Unity of command: Fayol's principles: strictly followed; Taylor's scientific management: not followed (functional foremanship). (iv) Basis of formation: Fayol's principles: personal experience; Taylor's scientific management: observations and experimentation.

items.stem: Explain any six limitations of planning.
items.answer: (i) Planning leads to rigidity: Managers may find it hard to change the plan. (ii) Planning may not work in a dynamic environment: The environment changes in ways the plan cannot foresee. (iii) Planning reduces creativity: Middle managers only carry out plans made at the top. (iv) Planning involves huge costs: Time and money are spent on preparing plans. (v) Planning is a time-consuming process: Little time may be left for implementation. (vi) Planning does not guarantee success: Success depends on proper implementation too.

items.stem: Explain any four ways and means of consumer protection.
items.answer: (i) Self-regulation by business: Firms set up customer service cells and follow ethical standards. (ii) Business associations: Bodies such as FICCI and CII lay down codes of conduct for members. (iii) Consumer awareness: An aware consumer can protect his or her own interests. (iv) Consumer organisations: They educate consumers and fight for their rights. (v) Government: It passes laws such as the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
